contexts.text: Overagainst () = not to behold, and yet still to behold. AC 2688.
Overagainst the flocks () = that they might be conjoined; namely, truths and goods to the natural; because it involves view, and thence excited affection...
Ye shall encamp overagainst it near the sea () = an influx of temptation thence. Overagainst = near so as to be in view; in the internal sense, that there may be influx thence. Explained.
Also the flock and herd shall not pasture overagainst this mountain (). Explained.
